title: Reconstruction from lower truncations on a ringed site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on it. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $E\in D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $V\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$, write $\Gamma(V,M)=M(V)$, regarded as an abelian group; define $R\Gamma(V,E)$ by applying $\Gamma(V,-)$ termwise to a K-injective resolution of $E$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and put $H^p(V,E)=H^p(R\Gamma(V,E))$. A module sheaf is placed in degree zero when this notation is applied to it.

Suppose there are an integer $d\geq0$ and a subset $\mathcal B\subseteq\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ such that every object of $\mathcal C$ has a covering by members of $\mathcal B$, and
$$H^p(V,\mathcal H^q(E))=0\qquad(V\in\mathcal B,\ p>d,\ q<0).$$
For $n\in\mathbf N$, put $E_n=\tau_{\geq-n}E$, with the canonical truncation maps $c_n:E\to E_n$ and transitions $f_n:E_{n+1}\to E_n$ [def-kun-truncations]. Then the product $P=\prod_{n\geq0}E_n$ exists in $D(\mathcal A)$, and there is a distinguished triangle
$$E\xrightarrow{(c_n)_n}P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\longrightarrow E[1],\qquad \operatorname{pr}_n s=f_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}.$$
Thus $E$, with its specified maps $c_n$, is a derived limit of its lower-truncation tower in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit].

proof.text: For every $n$, choose a K-injective resolution $E_n\to I_n$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The termwise product $\prod_n I_n$ exists: [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](2) gives sectionwise small limits of module sheaves, and the countable index set is small. By [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective] this product complex represents a product $P=\prod_n E_n$ in $D(\mathcal A)$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] to obtain a distinguished triangle $L\xrightarrow{p}P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\xrightarrow{\delta}L[1]$. Only clause (1) is used; no exactness of products of module sheaves is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0D6P and 0D6M, choice of the derived limit; Derived Categories Tags 0BK6 and 08TC

proof.text: The quotient maps defining good lower truncation [def-kun-truncations] satisfy $f_n c_{n+1}=c_n$. Let $a:E\to P$ be the product lift of $(c_n)_n$. Every projection of $(1-s)a$ is $c_n-f_nc_{n+1}=0$, so $(1-s)a=0$ by uniqueness in the product universal property. Exactness of Hom into the triangle [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact](ii), with $W=E$, supplies $c:E\to L$ such that $pc=a$. Write $p_n=\operatorname{pr}_np$; then $p_nc=c_n$ for every $n$. No uniqueness of $c$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0D6M, canonical comparison; Derived Categories Remark Tag 0H72 (compatible comparison, not a unique map)

proof.text: Apply the existing successive lower-truncation triangle [lem-pc-derived-lower-truncation-step-triangle] to E with integer n+1. It supplies the distinguished triangle H^(-n-1)(E)[n+1] -> E_(n+1) -> E_n -> H^(-n-1)(E)[n+2], with the specified canonical transition as middle arrow. The equality -((n+1):Z)+1=-n identifies its upper truncation index. This replaces a repeated complex-level kernel calculation and use of the short-exact-sequence triangle.

source.place: Tag 0D6M, successive-truncation triangle (Derived Categories Remark 13.12.4); explicit kernel calculation using good truncations

proof.text:
For every object $V$, evaluation followed by forgetting scalars is additive: kernels and addition are sectionwise in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The source has K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; so does $\operatorname{Ab}$, by applying that theorem to the one-object, identity-only site with the trivial topology and ring $\mathbf Z$. Therefore [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] applies to $\Gamma(V,-)$: $R\Gamma(V,-)$ preserves shifts and distinguished triangles. Apply it to step 3 and take the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. Fix $m\in\mathbf Z$ and choose a natural number $N\geq\max(0,-m,d-m+1)$. For $n\geq N$ and $V\in\mathcal B$, each of
$$H^{m+n}(V,\mathcal H^{-n-1}(E)),\quad H^{m+n+1}(V,\mathcal H^{-n-1}(E)),\quad H^{m+n+2}(V,\mathcal H^{-n-1}(E))$$
is zero: the sheaf index is negative and all three section-cohomology indices exceed $d$. In the long exact sequence these are the two outside terms for each of $H^{m-1}(V,f_n)$ and $H^m(V,f_n)$. Both maps are consequently isomorphisms. The same $N$ works for every $V\in\mathcal B$.

source.place: Tag 0D6M, last displayed three vanishing groups; uniform bound of Tag 0D6P

proof.text:
By [lem-kun-site-rgamma-derived-limit], applying $R\Gamma(V,-)$ to the triangle of step 1 gives a derived-limit triangle in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$, with the actual projection maps $R\Gamma(V,p_n)$. The Milnor short exact sequence [lem-pc-derived-limit-milnor-sequence] is therefore
$$0\to R^1\varprojlim_nH^{m-1}(V,E_n)\to H^m(V,L)\to\varprojlim_nH^m(V,E_n)\to0.$$
For $V\in\mathcal B$, step 4 and [lem-pc-derived-limit-eventually-iso] make its left term zero. Projection of the limit on the right to $H^m(V,E_N)$ is an isomorphism: an element at $N$ determines the later entries uniquely by the inverse transition isomorphisms, and the earlier entries by the transition maps. The composite is thus an isomorphism
$$H^m(V,p_N):H^m(V,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^m(V,E_N)\qquad(V\in\mathcal B).$$
The identification of this composite with the indicated map uses the projections in the cited derived-section triangle and the natural projection map in the Milnor sequence.

source.place: Tags 0D6M and 0D6L, local control of the limit projection; Tags 0D6K and 0BKX, derived-section Milnor sequence

proof.text: For any $T\in D(\mathcal A)$ let $\mathscr P_T^m$ be the abelian presheaf $V\mapsto H^m(V,T)$. Its sheafification is naturally the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal H^m(T)$. Indeed, represent $T$ by a K-injective complex $I$. The presheaf is the cohomology presheaf of the underlying abelian presheaf complex $I$; exact abelian sheafification, namely [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] with $R=\mathbf Z$, commutes with kernels, images and cokernels and fixes the terms $I^r$, which are already sheaves. Its resulting cohomology sheaf is the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal H^m(I)$ because forgetting module scalars is exact [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1). All maps used are induced on kernels and cokernels, hence this identification respects maps of complexes. For a derived morphism use a K-injective representative of the target and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] to represent it by a chain map; homotopic maps induce the same maps on cohomology. This proves the required naturality also for $p_N$.

source.place: Tag 0D6L, use of Tag 0BKV (cohomology sheaf as sheafification); explicit exact-sheafification argument on the underlying abelian complex

proof.text: The presheaf map $\mathscr P_L^m\to\mathscr P_{E_N}^m$ induced by $p_N$ is locally injective and locally surjective. To check either assertion on an object $U$, choose a covering $\{V_i\to U\}$ with $V_i\in\mathcal B$ as in the hypothesis. If two sections have the same image, their restrictions to each $V_i$ are equal by injectivity in step 5. Given a target section, restrict it to each $V_i$ and take its unique preimage using surjectivity in step 5. These are precisely the two local conditions of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective]. That theorem says the sheafified map is an isomorphism. Step 6 identifies it with the underlying abelian map of $\mathcal H^m(p_N)$, so $\mathcal H^m(p_N)$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves: the inverse of a bijective linear section map is linear and these inverses commute with restrictions.

source.place: Tags 0D6M and 0D6L, detection of the cohomology-sheaf map locally; with a uniform bound, both local injectivity and surjectivity follow

proof.text:
Since $N\geq-m$, [def-kun-truncations] identifies $\mathcal H^m(c_N)$ with the identity on $\mathcal H^m(E)$. The equation $p_Nc=c_N$ and step 7 give
$$\mathcal H^m(c)=\mathcal H^m(p_N)^{-1}\mathcal H^m(c_N),$$
so $\mathcal H^m(c)$ is an isomorphism. This holds for every integer $m$, even though $N$ was chosen separately for each $m$. To conclude in $D(\mathcal A)$, choose a complex representing $E$ and a K-injective representative of $L$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents $c$ by a chain map. That chain map is a quasi-isomorphism because all its cohomology maps are isomorphisms. It is inverted by the defining localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; hence $c$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0D6M, first paragraph and conclusion; Tag 0D6P

proof.text: Transport the distinguished triangle $L\xrightarrow pP\xrightarrow{1-s}P\xrightarrow\delta L[1]$ along the isomorphism $c:E\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ from step 8. Its arrows become $pc=a$, $1-s$, and $c[1]^{-1}\delta$. It is distinguished by invariance under isomorphism of triangles in [def-weil-triangulated-category]. The first arrow has projections $p_nc=c_n$ by step 2. This is exactly the triangle required by [def-weil-derived-limit], with $E$ and its specified truncation maps, rather than merely an abstract isomorphism between the first objects. The derived-limit definition is indexed from 1, so reindexing by the bijection n ↦ n+1 identifies its tower with the present n ≥ 0 tower, preserving every term and transition.

source.place: Tag 0D6P, conclusion; derived-limit triangle and transport along the compatible comparison
